title: Formal Security of Indifferentiable AEAD Against Strong Attacks
summary: The source indicates that ideal-AEAD propositions would yield strong related-key, KDM, and leakage resistance for indifferentiable AEAD, but their formal treatment remains open.

formal_statement.body: Open problem. Develop a formal treatment of the claim that an indifferentiable AEAD scheme resists strong forms of related-key, KDM, and leakage attacks. Specifically, formulate and establish security propositions for the ideal AEAD scheme over explicitly quantified classes of related-key-deriving, key-dependent-deriving, and leakage functions, and use those propositions to derive the claimed guarantees for indifferentiable AEAD schemes.

scope.domain: This concerns authenticated encryption and indifferentiability security under strong related-key, KDM, and leakage attacks.
parameters: Classes of related-key-deriving functions for related-key security
Classes of key-dependent-deriving functions for KDM security
Classes of leakage functions for leakage resilience
scope.unresolved_remainder: Formulate and establish security propositions for the ideal AEAD scheme over explicitly quantified classes of related-key-deriving, key-dependent-deriving, and leakage functions, then use those propositions to derive the claimed guarantees for indifferentiable AEAD schemes.

progress.summary: The source identifies analogous propositions for RKA, KDM, and leakage resilience of the ideal AEAD scheme as formulable over quantified function classes. It says these would imply resistance for indifferentiable AEAD schemes, while leaving the formal treatment to future work.
citation_labels: Manuel Barbosa et al., Indifferentiable Authenticated Encryption
